findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A mixed Python and JavaScript repo has `test = "pytest && npx vitest run && playwright test"` and a quick command containing `forge test --pytest {base}` plus a changed-only Vitest run. The picker rereads `test`, identifies the direct Playwright step as `browser`, and this filter removes it even when the picker runs for a pull request check or close. Before this change, the direct Playwright step was retained. Those checks now pass without the configured browser tests on every platform; the full run is unaffected.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A Windows quick command is `npm run unit 2>&1 && npm run test:e2e`, with `test:e2e` running Playwright. The operator scanner treats the ampersand in stderr redirection as a shell control operator, so this guard returns the whole command and the browser tests still run. The same misclassification occurs when `2>&1` is in the package script body. Both are valid redirections on an otherwise separate browser-test step.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A browser script has a pre-script that builds the app for a later API step, or a pull request uses the Python picker in a mixed Python/Vitest repo. The lifecycle case in `test_3` uses `NODE_SETTING`, which `skip_browser` returns untouched at `src/forge/fasttest.py:285`; it would pass even if browser classification dropped the build hook. `test_4` exercises no quick-test picker, so it also passes while the mixed picker removes a browser step from pull request and close runs. The cases likewise do not cover a browser step alongside `2>&1` redirection.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - An agent follows the synced combined-script guidance before proposing a quick command. The named proof checks the sentences in `GUIDE`, but that list contains no assertion that the agent limits only unit tests or runs the command once with the default branch as its base. Removing those instructions from both shipped guides would leave `test_2` passing, although it would no longer prove how to write and check the command.

The added parameter repeats the ordinary synced-guide assertions for an earlier-adopted repo. The repository's review rule calls for ordinary rules to be tested on a new repo and reserves earlier-release cases for behavior specific to old releases. Keep the new-repo case and remove this duplicate upgrade case.
